keyQuestions.text: How does Vibe run one task non-interactively: which prompt source, flags, output formats and exit codes does the headless contract expose?
Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?
What does Vibe read from the working directory and ~/.vibe/, and what would a generated repo-root .vibe/ mirror contain?
For each cli-opencode surface this repository uses, does Vibe have an equivalent, a partial equivalent or none, and what would porting take?
What would a cli-mistral-vibe deep-loop executor kind need, and is ACP a better dispatch surface than print mode?

keyFindings.text: `export.json` is a typed record, not a pile of logs: `vibe_version`, `outcome`, `stop_reason`, `error{message,code}`, `session_id`, `usage{input,output,cached,total}`, `cost_usd`, `steps`, redacted `config`, `warnings`, `started_at`/`ended_at`, `limits`, `subagents[]`, and a computed `exit_code`. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/app_server/run_export.py:117-160,178-238]

A denied tool has no exit code of its own. Headless runs cannot prompt for approval, and the binary carries "needs approval, which a headless run cannot give" followed by "denied": the denial is a tool result inside the run, so a run whose only problem was a denied tool can still end `finished` with exit 0. A caller that must detect denial has to read the journal/`export.json` or pin the tool set with `--enabled-tools`/`--disabled-tools` or an explicit approval agent. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/_bin/vibe-rs (strings: "needs approval, which a headless run cannot give", "denied")] [INFERENCE: based on the exit-code taxonomy in run_export.py:32-84 having no denial member, and on the denial being emitted as a tool result]

Architecturally `vibe` is a thin launcher, not the agent: `vibe/cli/launcher.py` `execvpe`s a bundled Rust binary (`vibe/_bin/vibe-rs`, Mach-O arm64) and points it at the installed `vibe-app-server` through `VIBE_APP_SERVER_BIN`. The Rust side owns the CLI and the headless loop (`src/headless_run.rs`, `src/headless/turn.rs`, `src/headless/report.rs` appear in the binary), and the Python side owns the app server, session journal and run export. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/cli/launcher.py:8-29,43-74,90-103] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/_bin/vibe-rs (strings: src/headless/*.rs)]

Exit codes are a fixed five-value taxonomy owned by `RunOutcome.exit_code`: `0` finished; `1` usage_error or config_error; `2` infrastructure_failure (model API after retries, or the runtime); `3` turn_limit, token_limit, price_limit, deadline, terminated, length or refusal; `4` aborted by an `--agent-socket` server. `--time-limit` is documented as "write the export and exit 3", which ties the documented timeout behaviour to the same taxonomy. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/app_server/run_export.py:32-84] [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/runtime-lifecycle/004-cli-mistral-vibe-creation/001-deep-research/research/evidence/vibe-help.txt:38-39]

Headless mode is entered with `-p`/`--prompt [PROMPT]`, and the prompt may come from the argument, from stdin, or from `--prompt-file PATH`; the same programmatic mode is mandatory for `--agent-socket` ("--agent-socket needs programmatic mode: pass -p or --prompt-file"). The help text says "--prompt-file ... instead of `-p` TEXT or stdin", while the binary also carries "Pass either -p TEXT or --prompt-file" and "No prompt provided for programmatic mode", so stdin-as-prompt is documented but not uniformly enforced. [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/runtime-lifecycle/004-cli-mistral-vibe-creation/001-deep-research/research/evidence/vibe-help.txt:28-41] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/_bin/vibe-rs (strings: "Pass either -p TEXT or --prompt-file", "No prompt provided for programmatic mode")]

Output is selectable: `--output text` (default), `json`, or `streaming`; `--output-dir DIR` additionally writes `export.json` and a copy of the session journal under `session/` on every exit. [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/runtime-lifecycle/004-cli-mistral-vibe-creation/001-deep-research/research/evidence/vibe-help.txt:30-31,44-45] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/app_server/run_export.py:1-6]

The bundled app server also offers a multiplexed surface: `--multiplex` serves "isolated Unified Harness connections in one stdio process", and the binary carries a `run-server` command that serves "many headless runs over JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout (experimental)" plus `--runs-per-app-server` to cap live runs. That is a second, long-lived dispatch seam beside one-process-per-run print mode. [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/runtime-lifecycle/004-cli-mistral-vibe-creation/001-deep-research/research/evidence/vibe-help.txt:82-95] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/_bin/vibe-rs (strings: "Serve many headless runs over JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout (experimental)", "--runs-per-app-server")]

The dispatch surface exposes explicit flags for every axis a governed executor needs: model `--model <ALIAS>` (headless-only, new sessions only), agent profile `--agent <NAME>` (builtin `ask`, `accept-edits`, `smart-approve`, `auto-approve`, or a custom `~/.vibe/agents/NAME.toml`), permissions `--auto-approve`/`--yolo`, `--smart-approve`, `--trust`, `--enabled-tools`, `--disabled-tools`, working directory `--workdir` (also `VIBE_CWD`) and `--add-dir`, and limits `--max-turns`, `--max-price`, `--max-tokens`, `--time-limit`. [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/runtime-lifecycle/004-cli-mistral-vibe-creation/001-deep-research/research/evidence/vibe-help.txt:17-67]

A Vibe dispatch has two credential families. The first-party `mistral` provider resolves a browser sign-in (OIDC against `https://console.mistral.ai`) or an API key from `MISTRAL_API_KEY`; any additional `[[providers]]` row is BYOK with its own `api_base` and `api_key_env_var`. First-party code prefers the active provider only when it is a Mistral provider, so a third-party credential never reaches a first-party endpoint. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/models.py:137-196] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/_defaults.py:9-19] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/platform_auth/_mistral.py:55-75]

Models are declarative rows too: `name`, `provider`, `alias`, `temperature` (default 0.2), `thinking`, `thinking_levels`, `input_price`/`output_price`/`cached_input_price` per million tokens, `max_context_length`, `auto_compact_threshold`, `supports_images`. Pinning `deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` and `zai-glm-5-3-flash` is therefore a provider row plus a model row each, selected by `--model <alias>`; Vibe compiles in no roster beyond the single default `mistral-medium-3.5` row. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/models.py:522-616] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:216-231]

Per-dispatch cost is locally computable even without the billing API: `export.json` carries `usage`, `cost_usd`, `steps` and `subagents[].cost_usd`, priced from the model row's per-million rates with cached input billed at `cached_input_price` when set. That gives a governed executor a cost signal per run, independent of the org budget endpoint. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/app_server/run_export.py:117-160,183-190] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/models.py:537-550]

Plan labels are derived from `/whoami`: chat plans map Free/Pro/Student/Team, Mistral Code maps "Free Codestral"/"Code Enterprise", and API plans map "Free API"/"PAYG API". The label is display data; the budget read above is the counter a dispatch actually draws on. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/setup/auth/whoami.py:346-390]

Providers are declarative, not a closed list: `ProviderConfig` carries `name`, `api_base`, `api_key_env_var`, browser-auth base URLs, `api_style` (default `openai`), `backend` (`mistral` or `generic`), `project_id`/`region` for Google Vertex ADC, `reasoning_field_name`, `emits_finish_reason` and `extra_headers`. The shipped defaults are only `mistral` and a local `llamacpp` endpoint, so any OpenAI-compatible gateway is a config row. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/models.py:137-204] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:200-214]

Reasoning effort has no dispatch flag. It is a per-model config field: `thinking` (a `ThinkingLevel`, default `off`) plus the offered `thinking_levels` list, with `thinking_is_set` distinguishing "unset" from "off" and the Mistral backend mapping curated level sets to its own reasoning-effort parameter. A governed executor must therefore pin reasoning through the model row or agent profile, not through the command line. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/models.py:551-616] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/llm/reasoning.py:17-62]

The Mistral-side catalogue is fetched, not shipped: `MODEL_CATALOG_PATH = "/model-catalog"` with surface `vibe-code`, a 5s bounded fetch and a 30-day cache TTL, built from the provider's `api_base`. A dispatch therefore sees whatever the configured Mistral API base advertises, while BYOK providers rely entirely on declared rows. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/model_catalog/_constants.py:1-27]

The usage counter is the org's monthly Vibe Code allowance. `GET /v1/billing/subscription` names the plan and whether pay-as-you-go covers the run past its allowance; `GET /v1/billing/budget` reports `usage_percentage`, `initial_budget`, `reset_at` and `payg_enabled` for the Vibe Code budget. Both are optional and read as `None` on a self-hosted platform or missing permission. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/app_server/_billing.py:1-46]

`AGENTS.md` is a real instruction surface on both levels: `$VIBE_HOME/AGENTS.md` is the user doc, and project docs are collected by walking up from the working directory to the open project root, outermost first, then rendered as one prompt section; a subdirectory `AGENTS.md` is injected lazily when a file below it is read. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/system_prompt.py:278-321] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/harness_files/_harness_manager.py:200-270]

Configuration is a layered stack: `user-toml` (`~/.vibe/config.toml`), `user-supplied`, `project-toml`, `environment` (`VIBE_*`), and session `overrides`, with an agent-profile layer allowed to change settings but forbidden from touching the three credential-routing base URLs (`vibe_base_url`, `console_base_url`, `vibe_code_sessions_base_url`) so an untrusted checkout cannot redirect a key. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/layers/agent_profile.py:20-44]

Custom agents are TOML profiles: `--agent NAME` resolves a builtin (`ask`, `accept-edits`, `smart-approve`, `auto-approve`) or `~/.vibe/agents/NAME.toml`, `.vibe/agents/` is discovered at the project root, `agent_paths` adds more directories, and `default_agent` defaults to `accept-edits` in both interactive and programmatic mode. [SOURCE: specs/cli-external-orchestration/runtime-lifecycle/004-cli-mistral-vibe-creation/001-deep-research/research/evidence/vibe-help.txt:46-47] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:876-910]

Project-local discovery is explicit and non-recursive. `find_local_config_dirs` inspects only the project root and collects `.vibe/tools/`, `.vibe/skills/`, `.vibe/plugins/`, `.vibe/agents/`, `.vibe/prompts/`, `.vibe/config.toml`, plus `.agents/skills/`. There is no `.vibe/commands/` directory in the discovery set. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/paths/_local_config_files.py:28-104]

Repo-mirror shape: today `.opencode/` carries `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/`, `plugins/`, `skills/`, `repo-rules/`, `scripts/` and `bin/`. The Vibe equivalent that discovery actually honours is `.vibe/config.toml` (providers, models, `default_agent`), `.vibe/agents/*.toml` (rendered from `.opencode/agents/*.md` and `.skilled/agents/*.md`), `.vibe/skills/` (rendered from `.skilled/skills/`), `.vibe/plugins/` (Vibe plugin format), `.vibe/prompts/` and `.vibe/tools/`. Command markdown has no `.vibe/commands/` counterpart and would have to become prompts or skills. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/paths/_local_config_files.py:28-104] [INFERENCE: based on this repository's `.opencode/` directory listing and Vibe's documented discovery set]

Skills load from `skill_paths` plus the discovered `.vibe/skills` and `.agents/skills`, filtered by `enabled_skills`/`disabled_skills` glob or `re:` patterns; the experimental registry mode pulls shared skills from Mistral and lets the project's skill win on a name collision. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:934-984]

The global home is a fixed tree: `$VIBE_HOME` holds `config.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, the global `.env`, `logs/` and `logs/session/`, `worktrees/`, `trusted_folders.toml`, `cache.toml`, `projects.toml`, `whoami_cache.json`, `model_catalog_cache.json` and the history file. None of these are repo-local, which is why a repo mirror must live in `.vibe/` rather than assume home-directory state. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/paths/_vibe_home.py:16-45]

The project config root is `.vibe/config.toml`. Vibe starts at the working directory and walks up parents until it finds a trusted `.vibe/config.toml`; an untrusted project config is ignored unless the dispatch passes `--trust`. That makes trust a per-dispatch gate for project configuration, not a one-time install setting. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/layers/project.py:14-25,44-70]

Custom agents: partial. Vibe has the concept and the roster: TOML profiles with `display_name`, `description`, `safety`, `agent_type`, `instructions` and arbitrary config `overrides`, discovered from `.vibe/agents`, `~/.vibe/agents` and `agent_paths`. The repository's agents are markdown with YAML frontmatter, so a renderer must map body→`instructions` and frontmatter→fields. Porting cost: low-medium per agent. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/agents/models.py:33-80]

Dispatch preflight hooks: partial, same mechanism as the spec gate. Vibe has `pre_tool` and `pre_agent`; the repository's dispatch audit and preflight plugins would become hook commands, and their per-dispatch state files would have to move under `.vibe/` or the packet. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/hooks/models.py:19-41] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/cli-dispatch-audit.js]

Executable OpenCode plugins have no Vibe equivalent. Vibe's plugin unit is a declarative `plugin.json` package, and its OpenCode adapter imports only portable Agent Skills and declarative MCP servers from an OpenCode package; OpenCode executables and custom tools are retained as package data and "never imported or evaluated" (`foreign_code_execution_unsupported`, `opencode_executable_tool_unsupported`). Porting the repository's 21 JavaScript plugins therefore means rewriting each as a Vibe artifact, not packaging them. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/plugins/_foreign.py:53-129,293-340] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/plugins/_native.py:924-947]

Goal and context bridges: partial. Context injection has a native equivalent (user and project `AGENTS.md` plus `.vibe/prompts`), but no goal-state surface exists, and the repository's goal plugin writes and reads a packet `goal.md` through OpenCode tool hooks. Porting cost: medium for context, high for goal state. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/system_prompt.py:278-321] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/opencode-goal.js]

Hook surface: Vibe declares seven hook types — `post_agent`, `pre_tool`, `post_tool`, `pre_agent`, `notification`, `session_start`, `session_end` — declared in `.vibe/hooks.toml` or `~/.vibe/hooks.toml`, with `strict` blocking allowed only on `pre_tool`, `post_tool` and `pre_agent`. The repository's plugins key off `tool.execute.before`/`after` and `session.*` events, so only the tool pair maps cleanly. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/hooks/models.py:19-41,80-100] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/harness_files/_harness_manager.py:140-143]

MCP Code Mode: none. Vibe's builtin tool set is bash, edit, grep, read_file, write_file, skill, task, todo, web_fetch, web_search and ask_user_question; there is no script/execute/notebook tool that would run TypeScript over MCP tools the way the repository's Code Mode does. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/tools/builtins (directory listing)]

MCP: equivalent. Vibe configures MCP servers as stdio or streamable-HTTP with static auth or OAuth and exposes their tools to the model; the repository's MCP routing plugin has no Vibe analogue, but the server contract itself ports by config. Porting cost: low. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/models.py:225-260] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/auth/mcp_oauth.py:1-40]

Permissions and the self-invocation guard: partial. Vibe has per-tool settings, approval agents with `SAFE`/`NEUTRAL`/`DESTRUCTIVE`/`SMART`/`YOLO` safety levels, `enable_auto_approve`, `bypass_tool_permissions` and a sandbox, which covers the permission model; a nested-CLI refusal would be a strict `pre_tool` hook rather than a dedicated guard. Porting cost: low for permissions, medium for the guard. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/agents.py:6-18] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:900-932]

Session-relaunch loop: none. The repository's relaunch plugin depends on `session.idle`, `session.compacted` and `session.resumed`; Vibe's hook set has `session_start`/`session_end`, `notification` and `post_agent`, with no idle, compaction or resume event. A Vibe port would need an external supervisor reading `export.json` outcomes rather than an in-process hook. Porting cost: high, and the loop's trigger semantics change. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/hooks/models.py:19-41] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/session-relaunch.js]

Skills: equivalent. Vibe parses YAML-frontmatter markdown (`parse_skill_markdown`) and discovers skills from `skill_paths`, `.vibe/skills` and `.agents/skills`, with enable/disable patterns. The repository's `SKILL.md` convention is the same format, so pointing `skill_paths` at `.skilled/skills` is the lowest-cost port in the whole comparison. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/skills/parser.py:116-153] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:934-960]

Slash commands: none. There is no `.vibe/commands` discovery; `.vibe/prompts` is a prompt-template directory resolved by `system_prompt_id`/utility prompt ids, not a user-invoked command catalogue with `$ARGUMENTS` substitution. Commands would have to become skills or prompts. Porting cost: high for the repository's command tree. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/paths/_local_config_files.py:28-104] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/prompts/__init__.py:63-100]

Spec gate: partial. A strict `pre_tool` hook runs a command before a tool executes and can block it, which is the same enforcement point the OpenCode spec gate uses, but the port needs a hook script plus a TOML declaration and the hook payload contract is not the OpenCode `tool.execute.before` shape. Porting cost: medium per guard. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/hooks/models.py:28-41] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/system-spec-gate.js]

Correction to Angle 4: Vibe **does** have a Code Mode equivalent. `run_typescript` is a runtime builtin program tool; calls a program makes carry `parent_call_id` pointing at the `run_typescript` call, and tool descriptions tell the model to page through data "from a `run_typescript` program as `tools.vibe.list_sessions`" and to reach subagents as `tools.subagent`. Iteration 4's "Code Mode: none" verdict is superseded by "equivalent, low-medium porting cost". [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/app_server/_session_peers.py:40-70] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mistralai_vibe_local_harness/protocol.py:1074-1093]

Discovery order is computed, not directory-walk order: `skill_paths` first (global scope), then project `.vibe/skills` and `.agents/skills`, then user-level skill dirs, deduped by resolved path; the first claimant of a name wins and the loser is reported as shadowed. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/skills/manager.py:228-275]

Registry skills are an opt-in second source: `experimental_enable_registry_skills` pulls shared workspace skills from Mistral with version pins and a reserved `latest` alias, materialised on disk and loaded beside local skills. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/skills/models.py:14-36] [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/config/vibe_schema.py:967-984]

Repository agents map with a renderer: body → `instructions`, frontmatter → `display_name`/`description`/`safety`, and deep-loop or review leaves get `agent_type = "subagent"` plus an entry in the `task` tool allowlist. The `main` name is reserved for hook matching and may not be used by a profile. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/agents/models.py:33-80]

Repository commands do **not** map one-to-one: `.opencode/commands/**/*.md` are argument-taking slash commands with `$ARGUMENTS` substitution, while Vibe's user-invocable unit is a skill whose body is instructions and has no documented argument placeholder. Converting a command to a skill preserves the workflow but loses argument interpolation. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/skills/models.py:72-90] [SOURCE: .opencode/commands]

Repository skills map with near-zero effort: point `skill_paths` at `.skilled/skills`, because every skill there is a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Extra repository frontmatter keys (`trigger_phrases`, `importance_tier`) are tolerated as `metadata`, and names such as `sk-code` satisfy the name pattern. [SOURCE: ~/.local/share/uv/tools/mistral-vibe/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vibe/core/skills/models.py:45-68] [INFERENCE: based on the `.skilled/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter read in earlier iterations and the parser's permissive metadata handling]

Skills are both model-invoked and user-invoked. The `skill` tool loads a named skill's full `<skill_content>` block plus a sample of its supporting files, and `user-invocable: false` hides a skill from the slash menu while `disable-model-invocation: true` makes it user-only. Reading the Python package as the CLI implementation: `launcher.py` only execs the Rust binary, so Python is the app-server/session half. The Rust parser has no local source in the wheel, only the help text and binary strings, so CLI-flag claims beyond those captures are `documented, unconfirmed`.

Treating `--output json` as the canonical machine record. It is the response channel; `export.json` is the run record. Building an executor around stdout JSON alone would lose `outcome`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `steps` and `exit_code`.

Answering the OpenCode-versus-Vibe counter comparison from client code. Both clients send a key to a provider; which internal counter the platform debits is server-side and unobservable locally. Recorded as UNKNOWN with the exact measurement that would settle it.

Reading `~/.vibe/config.toml` or any key to confirm the live provider: the directory holds only `trusted_folders.toml`, so there is no local provider state to observe, and reading a key value is out of scope by the angle's own rule.
Treating the model catalogue as a shipped roster: it is fetched from `/model-catalog` at runtime with a 5s cap and 30-day cache, so an offline install has only declared rows.
Assuming a `.vibe/commands/` directory: it is absent from `find_local_config_dirs`, so slash commands cannot be mirrored by dropping markdown into a commands folder.
Assuming project config applies by presence: `ProjectConfigLayer` requires trust, so the repo mirror must also be trusted per worktree (`--trust`) or it is inert.

Searching for a project-local plugin config file separate from `.vibe/config.toml`: plugin enablement (`enabled_plugins`/`disabled_plugins`) lives in the same layered config, so there is one config file to render, not two.
Looking for a Code Mode equivalent among builtin tools: the tool list has no script/execute member.
Looking for a Vibe command-markdown directory: none exists, and `.vibe/prompts` is resolved by prompt id, not by user invocation.
Mapping `session.compacted`/`session.idle` onto `post_agent`: the event timing and payload differ, so the relaunch loop's idempotency and context-withdrawal logic would not carry over.
Packaging the repository's `.opencode/plugins/*.js` as a Vibe plugin and expecting them to run: `_foreign.py` refuses executable OpenCode components by design.
Reading the `task` tool as an unrestricted subagent dispatch: its default allowlist contains only `explore`, so a custom subagent is invisible until the allowlist names it.
Searching for a command-argument templating feature in the skill parser: there is no `$ARGUMENTS` or equivalent placeholder in `SkillMetadata` or the skill tool.
Searching the builtin tool directory for a Code Mode tool: `run_typescript` lives in the Unified Harness runtime, not in `core/tools/builtins`, which is why the first pass missed it.

Treating the absence of `.vibe/commands` as proof that Vibe has no slash commands: user-invocable skills are the slash surface, so the correct verdict is "commands map to skills, without `$ARGUMENTS`".
Porting `completion-evidence` as a blocking hook: `post_agent` has no `strict`, so the port degrades to an advisory.
Searching the binary for a hook decision JSON schema: the decision protocol is not exposed as strings, so blocking is cited from the `strict` model contract rather than a wire format.
Searching the config schema for a sandbox mode: there is no field, so any "sandbox mode" claim would be documentation-only and is marked UNKNOWN for the CLI.
Treating `--auto-approve` as a sandbox: it suppresses prompts, and the only containment is `outside_workdir` plus protected-path escalation.
Guessing a `VIBE_SESSION_ID` env var for the session-env map: unobserved, and cli-devin deliberately omits its equivalent rather than inventing one.
Looking for a per-kind sandbox flag in Vibe: none exists, so `EXECUTOR_SANDBOX_IS_OS_BOUNDARY` must be `false` and containment must be post-hoc.
Looking for a Vibe web-search policy switch: the CLI has no such option, so the policy is `inherit`.
Mapping `reasoningEffort` to a Vibe flag: no such flag exists, so the field must be declared unsupported and the pin carried by the model row.

Adopting ACP as the first executor surface: it requires a protocol supervisor, a new completion signal and a permission answerer before a single iteration can run, while print mode runs on the existing contract.

Looking for ACP flags to pin a model or workdir: `vibe-acp` has no flags, so those come from config or from the session `new_session` payload, and the exact payload fields are UNKNOWN from the Python surface alone.
Looking for an ACP export path: none exists; export is a headless-only artifact.
Using `run-server` now: the binary itself labels it experimental.
